analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Coreweave beats; European Towers in focus; Datacentres Top of mind; Inwit & TI inline; ITV miss
key_insights: October core CPI rose 0.3% versus 0.2% expected, with broad-based strength in underlying components. The desk says it likely locks in a 25bp Fed hike in December, with one more in 1H27. The 10-year yield rose 10bp to 4.98%, and rate-sensitive pockets sold off.

Nvidia fell another ~6% on an independent investigation, NYT reporting and a possible House subpoena. The desk sees continued long-investor selling and little buying support. US lawmakers are also voicing opinions that could lead to tighter restrictions on Nvidia's China dealings.

Broadcom (+3.8%) and AMD (+0.8%) traded as primary beneficiaries of the Nvidia news. Volumes excluding Nvidia were light, with SPX constituents about 15% below normal. The desk rated floor activity 5 out of 10.

CoreWeave raised guidance as demand and backlog stayed strong, and customer prepayments are helping fund near-term needs. Shares rose about 5-7% after hours. Q3 revenue was $3.661b against a guide of $3.45b-$3.6b, and Q3 adjusted operating income was $379m against a $200-$260m guide.

CoreWeave management stepped back from issuing unsecured debt at current yields. The report reads this as continued funding stress for neoclouds despite the equity bounce. Pre-print 5-year CDS was about 1,150bp and bonds yielded above 15-16%. Hyperscaler 5-year CDS and bond spreads were largely unchanged.

CoreWeave's financing is clearer. It plans no further parent-level unsecured debt through 2027, with most remaining capex funded through DDTLs (delayed-draw term loans). New 4-5 year contracts price at $20-25mn/MW and estimated unlevered IRRs have risen to 20-30%.

Nebius and Cerebras report tomorrow, a further test of backlog quality and access to financing. The desk says credit markets will drive the group until CDS spreads and unsecured borrowing costs stabilise or fall meaningfully.

GS Top of Mind note on AI investment durability: AI spending will hold up, but credit quality will decide the winners. Hyperscalers are best placed, and neoclouds funding long-term commitments with uncertain revenues are more exposed. Gabriela Borges argues CoreWeave's wider CDS spreads reflect hedging rather than distress.

The report frames datacentre capex durability as a financing and power story and favours operators with secured capital and controlled power. SoftBank's $3.73bn write-down shows power scarcity can delay timelines, given multi-year turbine lead times and post-midterm uncertainty.
The desk flags an investor debate on what happens to the circular finance and backstop arrangements around Nvidia if Jensen Huang is no longer driving the company.

TSMC co-COO Kevin Zhang told the Nikkei Forum that leading-edge chip demand remains 'insatiable'. TSMC October sales were NT$586b (+15% MoM, +60% YoY), tracking at 34% of 4Q26 consensus, in line. The board approved an NT$9 per share dividend for 3Q26.

INWIT reported in-line 3Q26 results and reiterated 2026 guidance. Italian authorities including AGCOM are seeking to speed up resolution of its disputes with Swisscom and Telecom Italia. GS stresses this does not necessarily raise the odds of a favourable outcome, and expects a modestly positive share-price reaction.

Reportedly, Telefonica wants to renegotiate tower rents with American Tower, which bought its tower network for EUR7.7bn five years ago. El Confidencial puts the annual bill above EUR2bn, or 21% of operating profit. The desk notes Telefonica has renegotiated with tower companies before, so it is unclear whether this is new.

Telecom Italia's 3Q results were in line and guidance was reiterated. The FCF miss came from working capital phasing that should reverse in 4Q. GS expects investor focus on longer-term strategic questions such as Poste's recent stake build.

ITV missed and guided below as digital ad revenue slowed. 3Q26 revenue missed consensus by 1%, TV advertising fell 8% against guidance of about 5%, and 4Q advertising is guided down 5-10% against GS/consensus forecasts of 1.3%/1.8% declines. ITV announced GBP30mn of temporary 4Q savings.

GS cut ITV FY26/27 adjusted EPS by 2%/9%. It says consensus 2027 EPS could face double-digit downgrades but sees scope for a limited share-price reaction, because the weakness is confined to Media & Entertainment, whose sale to Sky remains on track for 2H27.

Infineon call: 2027 margin guide has upside, with mid-20s segment margin guided and supply, not demand, capping growth. Data centre revenue should reach about EUR4bn, SiC rises from about 700m to above 1bn, and multi-year supply arrangements and capacity reservations exceed EUR10bn in combined revenue volume.

GIR stays Neutral on TeamViewer after 3Q26. ARR and revenue missed, SMB is under pressure and Enterprise pipeline conversion is expected to slow in 4Q. FY26 ARR growth is cut to about -1% and revenue growth to about -2% YoY pro forma.

Sunrise investor questions focus on net cost savings, debt reduction and the meaning of 'inorganic options', ahead of a Ziggo spin-off. The short thesis rests on worsening negative cash flow and dividend funding, with net debt/EBITDA potentially nearing 5x by the end of next year.

Vodafone call centred on cost savings. The CFO said net savings would be well above EUR200mn. Andrew Lee sees significant further upside to the cost programme, while the author is more cautious given Germany's underlying performance. There was no comment on Xavier Niel's influence.

Freenet and Telefonica extended their term partnership with a signed term sheet. A final contract is expected by FY26. FY26 guidance is intact including a EUR50m negative GP/EBITDA impact, and a good final deal could create upside to Freenet's medium-term guidance.
Away from GS: JPMorgan upgraded SAP to Overweight and Berenberg raised Auto Trader to Buy from Hold.

Vodafone: CFO said net savings would be well above EUR200mn, and the CEO suggested they would approach a quarter of the current EUR1bn four-year target.

tension_points.bull_case: CoreWeave beat and raised, with contracts at $20-25mn/MW, unlevered IRRs of 20-30%, prepayments helping fund needs and no further parent-level unsecured debt through 2027. Gabriela Borges says wider CDS spreads reflect hedging and leading projects can still get financing.
tension_points.bear_case: Management stepped back from unsecured debt at current yields, bonds yield above 15-16% and high-yield AI issuance is slowing. Neoclouds funding long-term commitments with uncertain revenues are more exposed than hyperscalers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The CDS reaction to the CoreWeave print and tomorrow's Nebius and Cerebras results, which test backlog quality and access to financing. The credit view holds until CDS spreads and unsecured borrowing costs stabilise or fall meaningfully.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees scope for a limited share-price reaction because the weakness is confined to Media & Entertainment, whose sale to Sky remains on track for 2H27.
tension_points.bear_case: Consensus 2027 EPS could face double-digit downgrades after 4Q advertising guidance of down 5-10% against forecasts of 1.3%/1.8% declines.

tension_points.bull_case: Andrew Lee sees significant further upside to the cost-cutting programme. Net savings are well above EUR200mn and management left room for further upgrades.
tension_points.bear_case: The author is more cautious given Germany's underlying performance, with higher-margin mobile still weaker. Investors are likely to stay sceptical.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Organic service revenue growth turning positive and gross margins strengthening in Germany.
